gaps.note: The supplier certifications packet has no certification from the PV module supplier (requested August 1, 2026, not received), so supplier coverage for all manufactured products is incomplete.
The supplier certifications packet states that no material assistance cost ratio calculation has been prepared. That calculation is needed if the restrictions apply.

The transformer manufacturer's letter confirms a contract date and a manufacturing start date. It gives no information on the extent or cost of the off-site work, does not attach the binding contract terms, and does not address continuity after the transformer failed factory testing. All of this is needed to substantiate the off-site physical work claim.
The independent engineer's report expressly did not review the manufacturer's records. It gives no view on whether the off-site transformer work counts as physical work of a significant nature.

questions.prompt: When should construction be treated as having begun: in December 2025 based on off-site transformer manufacture, or January 12, 2026 based on on-site pile installation?
questions.context: A notice to proceed is not physical work. On-site work began January 12, 2026. The Seller relies on custom transformer manufacture starting December 22, 2025 under a contract dated December 10, 2025, supported only by a manufacturer letter. The independent engineer has not reviewed the manufacturer's records. The transformer later failed factory testing and is being rewound, which bears on continuity. The answer decides the domestic content threshold (45% vs 50%, against a computed 47.8%) and whether the foreign entity material assistance rules apply.

evidence.text: On-site physical work of a significant nature, beginning with pile installation for the tracker foundations, commenced on January 12, 2026.
commenced at our facility on December 22, 2025 and continued thereafter.
We have not reviewed the manufacturer's records and express no opinion on the tax treatment of off-site work.
If construction is determined to have begun in 2026, the applicable threshold would be 50% and the Project would not qualify at the computed adjusted percentage.
The sponsor's position is that the material assistance restrictions do not apply because construction began in 2025;

options.label: Accept a December 22, 2025 start based on off-site transformer work, conditioned on delivery of the contract, production records and continuity evidence
options.consequence: The domestic content bonus qualifies at 47.8% against the 45% threshold, and the material assistance rules do not apply. The credit rate stays at 50%, subject to the apprenticeship cure.

options.label: Treat construction as beginning January 12, 2026 with on-site pile installation
options.consequence: The domestic content bonus fails (47.8% vs 50%), reducing the rate to 40% and the credit to $54,560,000 on current basis. The material assistance rules apply and remain unverified until the module certification and cost ratio are delivered. Failing them eliminates the credit.

options.label: Defer the decision and make substantiation of the off-site work a condition precedent to signing
options.consequence: The construction start, domestic content bonus and foreign entity applicability stay open. Pricing and insurance sizing cannot be finalized until the documents are reviewed.
